summary: Transient 429s for long-polling/SSE sessions after enabling rate-smoothing on dedicated pool
description: Issue summary: After BrightLens enabled the new 'rate-smoothing' toggle for their dedicated pool and turned on per-route isolation via Console, they reported an increase in 429 responses for long-polling / SSE chat sessions. Impact: ~8% of active chat websocket/SSE connections experienced early 429s over a 45-minute window, causing degraded UX for real-time dashboards. Environment: Dedicated pool allocated to BrightLens, prod clusters in us-east and eu-west. Recent change: Console toggle 'rate-smoothing=v2' rolled out to their pool at 2026-03-13T09:12 UTC; canary rollout completed across both regions by 09:30 UTC. Steps to reproduce: 1) Open ~300 concurrent SSE sessions to the /v1/chat/stream endpoint with keepalive pings every 20s. 2) Send periodic user messages (avg 1 msg per session / 30s) with small-response models (redwood-chat-7b). 3) Observe token/accounting headers and response codes. Observed behavior: At ~09:35 UTC, 429s start appearing after 20-40s of activity; throttle headers indicate per-route token window exhausted despite overall tenant credits available. Expected behavior: Long-lived SSE sessions should see smoothing applied without premature per-route exhaustion; route-isolation should prevent unrelated bulk uploads from affecting live streams. Logs/snippets: - gateway logs show 429s with X-RateLimit-Reason: route_window_exhausted - token accounting snapshot (excerpt): route_window: 120/sec, tenant_remaining: 1.2M tokens, route_remaining: 0; several connections had keepalive pings counted as requests. Temporary workaround applied: Support recommended disabling 'per-route isolation' for this pool which reduced 429s (rolled back by BrightLens at 10:05 UTC).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a dedicated pool with per-route isolation and enable rate-smoothing=v2. 2) Start 200-400 SSE connections to /v1/chat/stream with periodic keepalives. 3) Send message bursts (~1 msg per session / 30s). 4) Monitor X-RateLimit-* headers and gateway logs for 429s.
observed_behavior: Short-lived 429 spikes for long-polling/SSE clients; headers indicate route_window_exhausted even when tenant credits remain. Keepalive pings appear in accounting and are being double-counted when smoothing transitions are active.
expected_behavior: Requests from long-lived sessions should be smoothed such that keepalive heartbeats do not prematurely deplete route windows; per-route isolation should only isolate heavy bulk ingestion routes and not penalize persistent SSE chat traffic.
investigation_notes: - Timeline: 09:12 UTC toggle enabled -> 09:30 UTC canary complete -> 09:35 UTC first 429s observed -> 10:05 UTC customer rolled back per-route isolation, 429s decreased. - Hypothesis 1: Rate-smoothing rollout changed refill algorithm; keepalive pings are treated as full weight (not lightweight) during transition window causing token bursts. - Hypothesis 2: Route isolation policy created narrow per-route windows and smoothing added an additional refill delay, causing temporary negative drift. - Evidence: Gateway trace shows keepalive (HTTP 200) followed by immediate token decrement; smoothing actor log includes a 'reconcile_delay' event around 09:34:58. - Repro on staging: Dev reproduced a version of the problem with synthetic SSE connections when using smoothing=v2 and route_min_window set < 200/sec. - Related: INT-4402 contains notes on smoothing reconcile logic and a patch in flight.
timeline: 2026-03-13T09:12 UTC - rate-smoothing=v2 enabled via Console. 2026-03-13T09:30 UTC - rollout completed for BrightLens pool. 2026-03-13T09:35 UTC - first customer report of 429s. 2026-03-13T09:50 UTC - Support escalated to SRE. 2026-03-13T10:05 UTC - Customer disabled per-route isolation; partial mitigation observed. 2026-03-14T02:14 UTC - SRE pushed a staging hotfix for smoothing reconcile logging.

root_cause: Under investigation. Current leading cause is a transient negative interaction between new rate-smoothing refill timing and narrow per-route windows that causes keepalive heartbeats to be accounted at full weight during reconciliation windows, depleting route token windows prematurely.
temporary_workaround: Disable per-route isolation for the affected pool or increase route_min_window to >= 500/sec; reduce keepalive frequency for SSE clients (e.g., 20s -> 60s) to reduce accounting churn.
resolution_plan: 1) Engineering to merge reconcile timing fix for smoothing actor (PR in review). 2) Run canary hotfix in staging against dedicated-pool simulation. 3) If verified, schedule emergency patch deployment to production with coordinated customer notifications. 4) Postmortem + console guidance: update UI to warn about combining route-isolation with smoothing=v2 for small route windows.
follow_up_actions: - Add telemetry to measure keepalive vs request weight during smoothing rollouts. - Update runbook to include recommendation to increase route_min_window before enabling smoothing in heavy-SSE customers. - Engineering to provide console guardrail and warnings.
